A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of StrandHead with matching core methods and experiments. The supplied v1 ends with references; v3 additionally contains supplementary Sections 6.1–6.6, which are included in this comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original head and hair generation results, quantitative comparisons in Table 2, a 30-volunteer preference study, hair-geometry statistics and ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and additionally reports FID/CLIP comparisons, controlled ablations, retrieval comparisons and failure cases.

M1.justification: The FLAME/DMTet head, neural scalp textures, prismatization, human-specific SDS/MSDS, geometric regularizers and strand-aware texture field already appear in v1. V3's three-stage organization separates existing operations; its expanded implementation descriptions do not establish a changed generation procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds explicit dreadlock and ponytail generation tests in Figure 10, extending qualitative coverage to difficult structured hairstyles. The USC-HairSalon analysis and 30-prompt head/hair benchmark remain; publishing the prompt list primarily adds documentation.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains HeadArtist, HeadStudio, HumanNorm and TECA for heads, and MVDream, GaussianDreamer, LucidDreamer, RichDreamer, TECA and HAAR for hair. Supplementary Table 3 reuses these comparator sets. Flux supplies FID reference images rather than a competing 3D method.

E3.justification: V3 adds supplementary FID evaluation against Flux-generated images and CLIP scoring, plus controlled sweeps of strand count, prism geometry and conditioning. These extend evaluation within the retained tasks; the main 30-prompt and 10-example/30-volunteer protocols are unchanged. Newly disclosed optimization budgets are documentation.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: human-specific versus general/no diffusion supervision, fixed-initialization prompt/head variations, FLAME-prior ablations, strand-count and prism-parameter sensitivity, geometry-loss ablations, nearest-neighbor comparisons and failure cases. Existing orientation, curvature, prismatization and texture analyses are retained or expanded across the main text and supplement.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and qualitative comparisons without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The volunteer count and descriptive hair-geometry statistics are retained; v3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All Table 2 scores are unchanged. V3 adds Table 3, reporting StrandHead FID/CLIP scores of 176.95/30.95 for heads and 201.19/27.84 for hair; hair CLIP remains below MVDream's 28.11. Extensive new ablation, retrieval and failure outcomes substantially expand the reported findings without demonstrating a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: V3 adds explicit mathematical specifications for the FLAME-fitting objective and SDF-based geometry penalties, and expands the MSDS gradient with a VGG-feature expression (Equations 17–21). These are limited formalization additions to existing components; the central prismatization and orientation/curvature mathematics remains unchanged.

C1.justification: V1 repeatedly claims generation without 3D/hair training data. V3 materially narrows this to avoiding large-scale hair–text paired data and acknowledges diffusion pretraining on human meshes. The abstract, introduction and conclusion also refocus the novelty claim on strand generation through human-specific 2D priors.

C2.justification: V3 adds concrete applicability limits: insufficient strand-generator expressiveness for dreadlocks/ponytails and high SDS computational cost. It also develops explanations of human-specific supervision, adaptation to bald heads, parameter robustness and generation beyond dataset retrieval. V1 lacks this breadth of mechanism and limitation discussion.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's framework/hardware descriptions, v3 supplies iteration budgets, loss weights, 3,000 strands with 100 points each, FLAME-fitting intervals, prism settings, initialization selection including HAAR-generated afros, runtime/memory requirements and the full prompt list. Sections 6.1–6.2 and 6.5 substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing that experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V3 makes its dependence on HumanNorm and its distinction from HAAR's paired-data training more explicit. It adds the VGG reference and removes several background bibliography entries, including SMPL, FaceVerse and NeuS. The main related-work categories and comparison landscape remain stable.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around human-centric priors. Method exposition is reorganized into bald-head, hair-geometry and hair-texture stages, with substantial detail moved into supplementary sections. The standalone Applications section is removed while application content remains elsewhere.

P2.justification: V3 substantially redesigns the teaser, pipeline, prismatization explanation and example gallery. V1's compact ablation display is split and redistributed, while new failure, sensitivity and diagnostic figures and Table 3 are added. Application illustrations remain in the teaser despite removal of the separate applications figure.

improvement.justification: V3 corrects a central overstatement about avoiding 3D training data, substantially documents previously underspecified implementation choices, and adds controls and concrete failure cases. Together these materially improve claim accuracy, reproducibility and understanding of applicability. The benefit comes from stronger evidence and transparency; the main comparison scores are unchanged, and empirical uncertainty remains unreported.
